newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ LEFT GAINS ASCENDANCY ACCORDING TO TV1 POLL.
newsitem.headline: NZ LEFT GAINS ASCENDANCY ACCORDING TO TV1 POLL.

text.p: New Zealand's left leaning Labour and Alliance parties have gained the ascendancy according to a TV1-Colmar Brunton poll published on Wednesday showed.
Together they would command 61 seats in the 120-seat parliament if an election was held now, the poll said.
Labour's support was steady on 42 percent while the Alliance gained two points to nine percent.
The ruling National Party was steady on 39 percent while its junior coalition partner fell one point to three percent.
The free-market ACT party was on just under five percent support, down one.

Labour leader Helen Clark was the preferred choice as prime minister with 25 percent support, up one point. National's Jim Bolger was steady on 20 percent and NZ First leader Winston Peters was down one on three percent.
Support for National Party senior minister Jenny Shipley rose four points to nine percent.
Disapproval of the government's performance was on 77 percent and approval on 14 percent.
